summary: Extended a panel-only suppressed-call check (step-0 entry 049, which found 0 of 20 non-PASS panel calls rare and protein-altering) to the whole genome, using the FILTER-tagged coding layer step 2 built. Of the 875 rare, protein-altering coding alleles found genome-wide, 129 sit in calls the variant caller marked non-PASS (dominated by low-mapping-quality and low-quality-by-depth filter reasons). Twenty-six genes only reach a candidate biallelic set if one of those filtered calls is rescued, and none of those 26 also carries a ClinVar pathogenic/loss-of-function allele or a top-30 phenotype rank. BUB1B itself carries zero non-PASS coding alleles.
why: A variant caller's FILTER column is tuned for a genome-wide false-positive rate, not for one child's disease allele, so a true disease variant sitting in a hard-to-map region is exactly the kind of call it would suppress. Checking this against the already-annotated callset by SQL costs hours; ruling it out by re-calling from the raw sequencing reads costs a day. It has to be ruled out before the BUB1B pair can be trusted as complete, rather than one allele of a bigger picture the filters are hiding.
verdict: H007 supported, committed at 0.80: no gene reaches a credible biallelic diagnosis only by rescuing a filtered call, and the BUB1B pair does not depend on any filter decision. H006 (retrospective) supported at 0.77: the panel's 20 filtered calls were correctly discarded, and the same conclusion holds at the coding-layer scale.

inherits.what: step 2's coding_alleles, coding_candidates and gene_biallelic tables keep every FILTER value rather than dropping non-PASS rows — the only reason this question could be asked genome-wide at no extra computational cost.

hands_to.what: step 5's read-level recovery of a partner allele was funded only conditionally, on step 6's oracle reply reporting one allele right and one wrong at rank 1 — a condition step 6's actual full-match reply closed, which is why step 5 never had to run.
